title: Longest Word With All Prefixes
statement:
Given a list of strings `words`, call a string in `words` *complete* when each of its non-empty prefixes (from its first letter up to the whole string) is also an entry of `words`. For example, `"app"` is complete only if `"a"`, `"ap"` and `"app"` all appear in `words`.

Return the longest complete string. If several complete strings have that greatest length, return the lexicographically smallest of them. If no string is complete, return the empty string `""`.
constraints: words[i] consists only of lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The direct check takes every word, cuts off each of its prefixes and looks it up in a set, which costs O(L²) per word of length L because each prefix is a new string. A trie stores all words so that the prefixes of a word are exactly the nodes on its path from the root. Marking the node where each word ends turns "is every prefix a word?" into "is every node on this path marked?", which is one walk of length L.

## Approach

1. Insert every word into the trie, creating child nodes as needed, and mark the last node with `isWord = true`.
2. Keep `best`, the best complete word so far, starting as `""`.
3. For each word, skip it at once if it is shorter than `best`, or the same length and not lexicographically smaller.
4. Otherwise walk its path from `root`; if any node on the way is not marked, the word is not complete.
5. If the walk finishes, the word beats `best`, so store it. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`words = ["k", "ki", "kir", "kira", "kiran"]` builds one path `k → i → r → a → n`, with every node marked.

- `"k"`: longer than `""`, its single node is marked, so `best = "k"`.
- `"ki"`, `"kir"`, `"kira"`: each is longer and every node on its path is marked, so `best` grows to `"kira"`.
- `"kiran"`: all five nodes are marked, so `best = "kiran"`, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(S), where S is the total number of letters: building the trie and checking all words each touch every letter at most once.
- Space: O(S) for the trie nodes.

## Pitfalls

- A one-letter word is always complete, so the answer is `""` only when no word has length 1.
- Ties on length go to the lexicographically smaller word, not the one that appears first.
- Duplicate words are allowed; they must not break the trie or the tie-break.
- Checking prefixes with `slice` and a set rebuilds each prefix and is quadratic for one long word.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `root` | the trie's empty root node |
| `node` | current trie node while inserting or checking |
| `ch` | current letter of the word |
| `isWord` | whether some word ends exactly at this node |
| `best` | longest (then smallest) complete word found so far |
| `complete` | whether every prefix of the current word is a word |

narration.2: Create the empty root of the trie; every word will hang below it.
narration.3: Insert each word into the trie.
narration.6: No child for this letter yet...
narration.9: Step down to the node for this letter.
narration.11: Mark the node where the word ends, so this prefix counts as a word.
narration.13: No complete word found yet, so the best answer starts empty.
narration.15: A word that is shorter, or equally long but not smaller, cannot beat best, so skip it.
narration.20: Walk the word's path; each node on it is one of its prefixes.
narration.22: This prefix is not in the list...
narration.27: Every prefix is a word and this word beats best...
narration.31: Return the longest complete word, smallest on ties, or the empty string.
